observations: Two mutations survive the suite, both on defensive branches the review's own findings did not name, and neither is a defect in the code as written. (1) backfillIndex's `case !written:` — a back-fill write that lost its compare-and-set still refuses to mark the bucket, which is right, but removing that branch reddens no test; the sibling branch, a refused write, is covered by TestABackfillWhoseRecordWriteIsRefusedLeavesTheIndexUnmarked. (2) openDue's stray-repair margin `at.Before(repairable)` — deleting it reddens no test, though it is what keeps the repair from taking an entry another sweeper has just written and is about to name. Each is one short test away from being pinned.

The stray margin is narrower than it reads: an entry is keyed to its minute, so one written at 10:00:59 is keyed 10:00 and is repairable at 10:02:30 rather than 10:02:59. The effective margin is cursorOverlap minus up to a minute, which is still far above the one KV round trip between an entry's write and its record's, so this is a note and not a finding.

Review minor 5 (Close cutting a record write short on a database that stopped answering) is sound by reading but I could not make it observable. I drove it live: envoy-dispatch against Postgres through a proxy I could stall, a sync held inside a GitHub call until its own two-minute deadline fired (the request returned 500 at elapsed_ms=120001, so failed()'s ctx.Err() branch did run), then SIGTERM. Head exited 15.10 s after SIGTERM and the d74ea872 control 15.12 s: the server's own bound for a stalled database (`exit with database connections still in use once the database stopped answering`, three failed probes) dominates, so no surface I can drive tells the two apart. The fix still releases the connection rather than leaning on that bound. That run was on the pod recreated at 01:10Z and its harness is gone with it.
